metadata.study title: Transcriptional analysis of liver from mice flown on the RR-6 mission
metadata.study funding agency: The sequencing analysis was funded by NASA Space Biology Program Office, Space Life and Physical Sciences Research and Applications Division.
study protocol description: A cohort of 36 weeks-old female C57BL/6 mice (Taconic Biosciences) were flown to the ISS and were housed in the Rodent Habitat. Half of the mice were subjected to microgravity for ~30 days and returned to earth alive before euthanization (Live Animal Return, LAR). The other half were subjected to microgravity for 52-55 days before euthanzing on ISS (Iss-Terminal, ISS-T).

All the animals from which the samples were processed in this dataset were operated to insert an implantable subcutaneous nanochannel delivery system prior to launch to deliver sham treatment. The cocktail included Propylene glycol (20%v/v), 1N HCL (10%v/v), Solutol HS 15 (10%v/v), 1N NaOH (5%v/v), PBS (12.5%v/v), and water (42.5%v/v).

The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol (Protocol number RR6) was approved on Oct. 24, 2017 by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
After ~30 days in microgravity, half ot the mice returned to earth alive (LAR Flight) and were euthanized by Isoflurane inhalation and were dissected immediately at Novartis Facilities.

The other half of mice were euthanized on ISS (ISS-Terminal Flight) by intraperitoneal injection of ketamine/xylazine/acepromazine after ~60 days in microgravity. Following blood draw and hind limb dissection, the carcasses were wrapped in aluminum foil, placed in a ziploc bag and placed in storage at -80C or colder until return to earth and dissected at Houston at a later date.

There were two Baseline groups of animals sacrificed (LAR Baseline & ISS-T Baseline) at Kennedy Space Center. A Ground Control group (LAR Ground Control) mimicked the LAR Flight group, which was housed at KSC, then shipped alive to Novartis Facilities, where both the LAR Flight and LAR Ground Control groups were processed.

The ISS-Terminal Ground Controls, housed at KSC, followed the same euthanasia timeline, methods, and preservation of the ISS-Terminal Flight. The final dissection of frozen 60-day ISS-Terminal Flight, frozen 60-day ISS-Terminal Ground Controls and 0-day FLT baseline anmials were completed at Houston Methodist Research Institute, in Houston, Texas. For all ISS-T groups, on the day of dissection, the frozen carcasses were removed from -80C freezer and placed in 4C fridge for thawing prior to dissection.

Multiple tissues were collected from each carcass by Primary PI and NASA BSP. All the liver tissues used for extraction in this dataset were preserved in liquid nitrogen after dissection and stored at -80C.
The frozen preserved tissues were shipped frozen to NASA Ames Research Center and handled by LSDA.

RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA). Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 30 mg of frozen tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed and immediately placed in 600 uL of the Buffer RLT solution. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix (Zirconium Oxide 2.0mm Beads, Next Advance) on Bullet Blender Gold 24 (Next Advance) for 5 minutes at 4C. Homogenates were centrifuged for 3 minutes at RT and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify RNA following the manufacturer protocol.
RNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse free H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA).
RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with the Agilent RNA 6000 Nano Kit or Agilent RNA 6000 Pico Kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA).
ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA Cat
4456739, v92) at 1:100 dilution of either Mix 1 or Mix 2 were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol.

RNA ribo depletion was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold. Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters were 1.5 uM (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size ~300 bp was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). Pooled library concentration was measured by Universal qPCR Master Mix (Kapa Biosystems, Wilmington, MA). Library quality control was determined by iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA).
RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Paired end 149bp. PhiX included as control.

Raw fastq files were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.0.0). Raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1) and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports.

Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
metadata.study publication title: Counteracting Muscle Atrophy on Earth and in Space via Nanofluidics Delivery of Formoterol
metadata.study description: The objective of the Rodent Research-6 (RR-6) study was to evaluate muscle atrophy in mice during spaceflight and to test the efficacy of a novel therapeutic to mitigate muscle wasting. The experiment involved an implantable subcutaneous nanochannel delivery system (nDS; between scapula), which delivered the drug formoterol (FMT; a selective Beta-2 adrenoceptor agonist), over the course of time. To this end, a cohort of forty 32-weeks-old female C57BL/6NTac mice were either sham operated or implanted with vehicle or treatment-filled nDS, launched in two Transporters (20 mice per Transporter) on SpaceX-13 on December 15, 2017. They were transferred to Rodent Habitats onboard the International Space Station (ISS), and maintained in microgravity for 29 days (N equals 20, Live Animal Return [LAR]), or greater than 50 days (N equals 20, ISS Terminal). After 29 days, the 20 LAR animals were returned live to back to Earth on January 13, 2018,. After splashdown, the animals were ambulatory on-ground for ~4 days, until all subjects were processed during one day of dissections. There were two Baseline groups of animals sacrificed (LAR Baseline and FLT Baseline; N equals 20; 40 animals; ~36 weeks old) at Kennedy Space Center (KSC; 12/9/17). A Ground Control group mimicked the Flight LAR group, which was housed at KSC, then shipped alive to Novartis' Facilities, where both the LAR and LAR Ground Control groups were processed (~41 weeks old; 1/16/18). All were anesthetized with isoflurane, blood samples were obtained by closed-chest cardiac puncture, and the animals were euthanized by exsanguination and thoracotomy. The 20 ISS Terminal mice were anesthetized via intraperitoneal injection of ketamine/xylazine/acepromazine over the course of a four days of dissections (2/6/18 until 2/9/18; 53-56 days after launch; 44 weeks old at time of on-orbit dissections). Blood samples and euthanasia were conducted the same as LAR and Baseline. Following blood draw and hind limb dissection, the ISS-terminal animal carcasses were wrapped in aluminum foil, placed in a ziploc bag and placed in storage at -80C or colder until return. The ISS-terminal Ground Controls (at KSC) followed the same euthanasia timeline, methods, and preservation. The final processing of frozen ISS-terminal, frozen ISS-terminal Ground Controls and frozen 0-day FLT baseline animals were completed at Houston Methodist Research Institute, in Houston, TX (5/21/18 until 5/24/18). GeneLab received samples of liver from only sham treated animals (no drug treated animals) from the following groups Flight: LAR (N equals 10), ISS Terminal (N equals 10); Ground Controls: LAR GC (N equals 9), ISS Terminal GC (N equals 10), LAR Baseline (N equals 10) ISS Terminal Baseline (N equals 10). Total RNA was extracted and sequenced at a target depth of 60 M clusters per sample (ribodepleted, paired end 150).
